description: Machine-readable index of rules that must be backed by RedCap revival, hook, validator, or explicit manual-review safeguards.

strength_tiers.label: 物理强保障
strength_tiers.meaning: 规则已经绑到 repo-owned script、validator、hook、CI 或 fail-closed runtime chain，命中时可被确定性执行或阻断。

strength_tiers.label: 宿主耦合保障
strength_tiers.meaning: 规则是否成立取决于当前宿主是否暴露 session、hook、binding 或其它控制点；需要结合 host capability matrix 判断。

strength_tiers.label: 人工/宿主边界保障
strength_tiers.meaning: 规则已被登记、审计和诊断，但当前没有 repo-owned veto 点；只能诚实标注为 host-limited 或 manual-only。

tier_interpretation.scripted: 通常落在 G1；若依赖宿主接线，则需结合 host capability matrix 判断是否退到 G2。
tier_interpretation.hooked: 通常落在 G1 或 G2，取决于宿主是否真正提供并验证了对应 Hook。
tier_interpretation.validator: 通常落在 G1，因为规则已进入 fail-closed 校验链。
tier_interpretation.manual-only: 落在 G3，必须说明为什么当前不能安全自动化。
tier_interpretation.documented: 仅文档声明不足以宣称强保障，至少属于待补强边界。
tier_interpretation.not-automatable: 落在 G3，且必须写清不自动化的原因。

guarantees.rule: Every RedCap guarantee surface must be audited against the Evolution-grade baseline: automatic trigger, evidence ledger, candidate handling, independent review, promotion or close decision, and visible failure state.
guarantees.automation: redcap-evolution-grade-check validates the R0 registry and redcap-diagnose/spec-check consume it so degraded or host-limited guarantees stay visible instead of becoming invisible local patches.

guarantees.rule: High-value user corrections, repeated failure modes, identity-growth signals, skill candidates, and governance-rule changes must be captured as Evolution candidates before they are promoted or explicitly closed.
guarantees.automation: redcap-evolution-candidate-check validates candidate shape and can run in strict mode before final closeout to reject unresolved candidates.

guarantees.rule: Governance tranches must explicitly report how Evolution candidates were handled; closeout must block when the task report omits candidate handling or strict candidates fail.
guarantees.automation: redcap-evolution-harvest-check validates governance task reports and closeout runtime runs it before receipt generation.

guarantees.rule: RedCap-native capabilities, host-exported skills, and portable skill packages must share a single source of truth; host entries may be thin startup indexes but must not fork the rule body.
guarantees.automation: redcap-skill-lifecycle-check validates the single-source skill lifecycle policy and rejects host entries that directly import large rule bodies or omit revive/core anchors.

guarantees.rule: Old task reports, specs, task cards, knowledge records, and ignored runtime evidence must declare preserve, archive, translate, prune-when-safe, or ignore-runtime lifecycle behavior before they are cleaned or reused.
guarantees.automation: redcap-legacy-asset-lifecycle-check validates the lifecycle policy and ensures prism/runs has no safe-to-prune acceptance fixture residue before closeout claims the residue is under control.

guarantees.rule: New sessions must restore identity, soul, CONTRIBUTING, lessons, design principles, and the current task anchor before doing work.
guarantees.automation: redcap-revival-check validates the revival protocol and host entry files.

guarantees.rule: After re-anchor, the host must obtain a compact current-state view before explaining status or continuing work.
guarantees.automation: redcap-current-status.sh remains the required first-read status surface. SessionStart-capable hosts now invoke the installer, which runs current-status physically during startup; Codex.app and other startup-import-only hosts still rely on explicit installer/current-status execution.
guarantees.non_automation_reason: Not every host exposes SessionStart hooks. Codex.app still provides startup import without repo-owned hook execution, so RedCap cannot claim this rule is automatic everywhere.

guarantees.rule: Revival must reload the anti-degradation rule map so long tasks do not lose hook, reporting, Prism, or closure constraints.
guarantees.automation: revival-check requires an on_session_revival reload checkpoint.

guarantees.rule: Status replies, final summaries, task reports, and notifications must start from the four human-readable status lines; repo-tracked task reports must also explain terms, completion level, and receipt evidence without stale next-step claims.
guarantees.automation: redcap-current-status.sh emits the four-line shape; task-report-check validates task-report summaries and delegates formal task-report wording quality to redcap-human-output-quality-check.sh. Live chat replies remain host-limited and must be reviewed rather than claimed as fully machine-enforced.

guarantees.rule: Framework changes must review lessons and design principles before implementation.
guarantees.automation: revival protocol requires lessons; execution-guarantees check keeps the rule in the protected map.

guarantees.rule: After each meaningful change, new failure modes, corrected assumptions, and reusable methods must be considered for lessons.
guarantees.automation: task report template and stop-review require explicit lesson consideration; quality of the lesson remains human-reviewable.

guarantees.rule: Knowledge archaeology must start from compass/knowledge/index.md and open only the specific knowledge files needed for the task.
guarantees.automation: redcap-knowledge-index-check.sh ensures every top-level knowledge markdown file is represented in the first-read index; spec-check consumes it.

guarantees.rule: RedCap must keep a human-readable workflow panorama so users and future agents can understand the whole framework before diving into script names.
guarantees.automation: redcap-mechanism-vitality-check.sh verifies the panorama surfaces exist and contain the core Layer A, Layer B, Prism, planning-review, closeout, and legacy-governance concepts.

guarantees.rule: Cap identity and collaboration posture must be restored at session start when the identity file exists.
guarantees.automation: revival-check verifies host entries explicitly point at ~/.cap/identity.md as the personal soul anchor, while soul.md and the installer remain the shared revival contract.

guarantees.rule: Identity updates must be committed and pushed immediately, but the content decision should remain intentional and human-visible.
guarantees.automation: Repository gates can check that the rule is documented, but should not auto-edit or auto-push a personal identity file.
guarantees.non_automation_reason: Identity content is personal memory; automatic mutation or push would risk corrupting the user's chosen identity record.

guarantees.rule: Cap revival and RedCap workflow import must have a single installer entry so hosts and humans can re-anchor with one command instead of reassembling the workflow from memory.
guarantees.automation: redcap-install.sh performs identity bootstrap, current-status, tracking-health, host-hook-readiness, execution-guarantee, and revival checks; revival-check ensures the installer is referenced by host entry surfaces, and Layer B SessionStart now invokes the installer on hosts that expose that hook.

guarantees.rule: Formal Prism work must use dispatch-check, run-scoped session registry, schema collection, synthesis audit, adjudication, and archive checks.
guarantees.automation: Prism tools validate dispatch and archive; execution guarantees keep these requirements in the protected map.

guarantees.rule: Every RedCap-owned Prism dispatch must consume a fresh, provenance-aware agent availability cache with a one-hour TTL and reject provider-unqualified or currently unavailable Agent rosters before launch.
guarantees.automation: prism-availability refreshes compass/.workflow/prism-agent-availability.json when stale, too weak, or generated under a different root/probe/provider-policy/PATH provenance; probe and provider-policy content hashes are part of provenance. dispatch-check calls check-roster before role/diversity checks, and diagnose/spec-check surface cache health.

guarantees.rule: Before delegating to Prism workers, the coordinator must distinguish install/config cache from real headless health, honor provider freeze windows, and record degradations honestly.
guarantees.automation: redcap-detect-agents refreshes registry without calling frozen providers; redcap-agent-health-probe reports frozen without executing live commands; prism-dispatch-check and redcap-provider-policy block frozen providers in RedCap-owned launch paths.
guarantees.non_automation_reason: Real headless probes can spend quota, hit login prompts, or require user credentials; they should be explicit diagnostics, not unconditional hooks.

guarantees.rule: Session start and fallback paths must refresh the local agent registry without treating it as proof of auth or rate-limit health.
guarantees.automation: redcap-detect-agents is the canonical registry refresh script.

guarantees.rule: Host overlay skills must remain advisory and must not turn already-authorized RedCap work into ask_user, need_user, blocked, or downstream-skill handoff blockers.
guarantees.automation: redcap-overlay-governance-check.sh verifies RedCap-owned overlay/ask_user boundaries and spec-check consumes it.

guarantees.rule: RedCap must provide a single diagnostic entry that summarizes current status and runs the key governance checks without requiring manual script hunting.
guarantees.automation: redcap-diagnose.sh runs current-status plus docs, knowledge, overlay, execution, revival, and spec checks through the read-only-safe first-read chain; host startup automation still depends on the current host's hook surface.

guarantees.rule: RedCap must surface whether .dev-task, task report, and explore-notes tracking assets are still present and aligned, instead of waiting for tracking drift to be discovered by accident.
guarantees.automation: redcap-tracking-health.sh audits the current task anchor, task report binding, and explore-notes inventory; current-status and diagnose surface it directly.

guarantees.rule: The scribe and scratchpad layer must be visible to runtime diagnostics so explore-notes, PM Gate input, and tracking drift do not silently become zero-work mechanisms.
guarantees.automation: redcap-mechanism-vitality-check.sh and redcap-tracking-health.sh jointly verify that explore-notes stays tied to PM Gate input and that stale scratchpad entries are surfaced by diagnose/spec-check.

guarantees.rule: When new work enters the Layer B execution flow, the current task card must be re-anchored and all tracked, staged, and untracked workspace changes must stay inside the task card's allowed modification scope.
guarantees.automation: redcap-drift-check.sh validates the current task metadata and allowed modification scope, including untracked files, so new reports or docs cannot escape the active task card while an old receipt remains misleadingly green.

guarantees.rule: Layer B PM Gate must explicitly compare the user's original intent against confirmed requirements and completion standards so strategic goals cannot be silently narrowed into a route-only or partial task without a visible boundary.
guarantees.automation: redcap-intent-coverage-check.sh validates the task-card coverage section; redcap-pm-gate-check.sh consumes it as part of PM Gate, and diagnose surfaces it as a visible control gate.

guarantees.rule: Documented FSM states and communication status values must stay aligned with the scripts that validate state.yaml.
guarantees.automation: redcap-state-machine-check.sh compares documented FSM states with redcap-check-state.sh and is consumed by spec-check.

guarantees.rule: Layer B distributed control-plane lifecycle and runtime-memory terminology must stay aligned with the scripts, ledgers, and entry documents that actually implement them.
guarantees.automation: redcap-layerb-lifecycle-check.sh verifies the lifecycle contract, glossary surface, referenced script files, guarantee registration, and key entry wording; diagnose consumes it directly.

guarantees.rule: Layer B terminal closeout must run through the unified closeout runtime so agent promises, Prism acceptance, receipt, summary, blocker carry-forward, and rescue audit are checked as one transaction.
guarantees.automation: redcap-layerb-closeout-runtime-check.sh validates the runtime entry, promise-ledger section, Prism acceptance gate, and audit-open path; redcap-diagnose.sh now provides the diagnose-rescue strong entry, and task-complete guard calls the runtime instead of invoking ad-hoc closeout steps.

guarantees.rule: Layer B completed truth must be fail-closed: authors may not declare completed unless Prism acceptance is valid, receipt exists, and pending closure is clear.
guarantees.automation: redcap-prism-acceptance-bind/check enforce that independent acceptance is bound to the current task_id + confirmed_hash, redcap-layerb-fsm/current-status surface lifecycle state honestly, and closeout runtime refuses completed when acceptance or receipt conditions are missing.

guarantees.rule: Layer B plans that shape multi-step implementation must pass through an explicit PLANNING and PLANNING_REVIEW control state before execution unless the task is intentionally classified as light work.
guarantees.automation: redcap-layerb-fsm-check.sh keeps the PLANNING and PLANNING_REVIEW states aligned with the lifecycle docs; redcap-mechanism-vitality-check.sh keeps the planning-review gate visible in diagnose/spec-check.

guarantees.rule: Layer B mid-task user changes must be captured as U<n> ledger rows, replanned before execution resumes, explained in a user-visible replan decision summary, and prevented from closing a child task as if the parent task were complete.
guarantees.automation: redcap-change-intake-check validates the inserted-requirement ledger, unresolved U items, replan updates, required replan decision summaries, and parent_completion_claim; PM Gate, diagnose, spec-check, current-status, and Layer B FSM checks consume the gate.

guarantees.rule: Layer B completion requires physical task report evidence, unified closeout runtime consumption, Prism acceptance, receipt generation, and pending-closure honesty.
guarantees.automation: task-report-check, Prism acceptance binding/check, unified closeout runtime, and session-end jointly require task report evidence, promise-ledger reconciliation, receipt generation, and honest blocker carry-forward without clobbering pre-existing blockers.

guarantees.rule: Docs archaeology must start from catalog, and docs changes must regenerate and check the catalog.
guarantees.automation: redcap-docs-catalog.sh check is consumed by spec-check, and the summary/plan/check/retention commands no longer depend on temporary writable files.

guarantees.rule: Docs archaeology must use summary/plan/budget progressive disclosure before opening source documents, and bulk directory reads must fail closed by default.
guarantees.automation: redcap-docs-catalog.sh plan selects candidates from summaries, budget rejects directories, glob-like paths, uncataloged paths, too many files, and oversized read sets; acceptance covers the behavior.

guarantees.rule: Critical RedCap runtime, Prism, knowledge, host-adapter, and product-shape files must be discoverable through the File Lookup Dictionary without requiring a bulk repository read.
guarantees.automation: redcap-file-lookup-dictionary-check validates required path coverage and broken dictionary links; spec-check and diagnose consume it as a fail-closed control-plane gate.

guarantees.rule: Shared knowledge and sedimentation output must have an independent repository shape, per-user namespace, append-only entries, index-first retrieval, and exact duplicate rejection before RedCap treats it as a scalable team memory layer.
guarantees.automation: redcap-shared-knowledge provides init, append, index, dedupe, and check commands; shared-knowledge-check, spec-check, and diagnose keep the local template and append-only contract visible.

guarantees.rule: The public shared-knowledge repository may be considered bound only when a machine-readable remote binding policy lists the exact safe template candidates, rejects credentials and private RedCap surfaces, and can verify the remote branch head in explicit live mode.
guarantees.automation: redcap-shared-knowledge-remote-check validates the local policy and candidate safety by default; explicit --live verifies the Gitee branch head, remote tree, and candidate file content without making every spec-check depend on network availability.

guarantees.rule: RedCap must keep catalog + rg + metadata as the default retrieval route until shared-knowledge scale or measured retrieval failures cross explicit thresholds; RAG or GraphRAG must never be enabled because it is fashionable or by default corpus loading.
guarantees.automation: redcap-retrieval-escalation-check validates current route, thresholds, forbidden full-corpus defaults, docs catalog scale, and shared-knowledge / redcap-arsenal entry counts; spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance consume it as a fail-closed gate.

guarantees.rule: First-start revival must initialize or verify the local user namespace, Cap agent identity summary, and shared-knowledge user directory without committing private identity text into the RedCap repository.
guarantees.automation: redcap-install runs redcap-user-agent-identity init during revive; redcap-user-agent-identity check is consumed by spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance.

guarantees.rule: RedCap-owned Feishu notifications must use the single reachable lark-cli profile cli_a9579f5b12219bb5 and may only fire for node reports or human-intervention interrupts; webhook, old profiles, followup watchers, and duplicate success notifications are forbidden production paths.
guarantees.automation: redcap-feishu-notification-policy-check validates the policy, source call sites, and ignored local config; spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance consume it.
guarantees.runtime_limitation: The checker can prove RedCap will not use another profile, but a real send still requires the user to register profile cli_a9579f5b12219bb5 in the local lark-cli configuration.

guarantees.rule: Before RedCap is packaged as npm, portable runtime, or any public distribution, the exact package candidate file set must pass a fail-closed safety audit that rejects local secrets, host-private entry files, runtime evidence, and credential-like content.
guarantees.automation: redcap-package-publish-safety-check validates the default future package surface and can audit explicit package file lists; spec-check, diagnose, CLI facade, and acceptance consume it before RedCap may claim package readiness.

guarantees.rule: RedCap may claim runtime / CLI / package readiness only when a machine-readable package policy generates an exact candidate file list and that list passes the package safety gate.
guarantees.automation: redcap-runtime-package-manifest.sh validates package.json, publish_allowed=false, required files, candidate glob expansion, and package safety against the generated candidate list; spec-check, diagnose, CLI facade, and acceptance consume it.

guarantees.rule: Any control-plane check consumed by a higher-level validator must propagate failures to the parent validator result.
guarantees.automation: redcap-spec-check wraps docs catalog, execution guarantee, and revival checks with explicit fail-closed handling; acceptance simulates all three failing routes.

guarantees.rule: Host-specific hooks must converge into Layer A/Layer B shared session-start, stop-review, on-complete, and session-end control scripts.
guarantees.automation: session-start/session-end scripts and validator-chain provide the shared control path; SessionStart-capable hosts now also run the installer through redcap-layerB-session-start.sh, while hook standards define host alignment.

guarantees.rule: When a task is already authorized and no real human gate is hit, the main agent must not interrupt merely out of caution; if the host cannot offer reply-time veto, RedCap must mark this boundary as host-limited instead of pretending it is physically enforced.
guarantees.automation: Current Codex.app and similar hosts expose startup import but not repo-owned reply veto; execution guarantees and host capability docs must therefore describe this as host-limited rather than auto-enforced.
guarantees.non_automation_reason: The decision to pause, ask the user, or hesitate before commit happens inside the host agent's live reply path. Without a repo-owned pre-reply veto API, RedCap can document, audit, and diagnose this boundary but cannot physically intercept every violation.

guarantees.rule: Agents must use the acceptance case index before opening the giant multi-session acceptance script, so case lookup stays targeted and does not flood context.
guarantees.automation: redcap-acceptance-index.sh provides summary/find/check without temporary writable files, and token-risk audit requires it as the mitigation for the large acceptance suite.

guarantees.rule: New sessions and framework changes must not reintroduce large-file auto-imports, unguarded giant tracked files, or unmanaged ignored runtime directories that can flood agent context.
guarantees.automation: redcap-token-risk-audit.sh checks entry files, tracked large files, ignored runtime directories, and required navigation mitigations; spec-check and diagnose consume it through the read-only-safe first-read chain.

guarantees.rule: CONTRIBUTING remains the authoritative full specification, but new sessions and reviewers must first consume the compact core contract and route to exact sections instead of default full-context injection.
guarantees.automation: redcap-contributing-ia-check.sh validates core size, entry imports, Copilot startup rules, and stop-review selected-section prompts; token-risk audit prevents full auto-import regression.

guarantees.rule: Layer B governance changes must be reviewable through explicit architecture, governance, and contracts tracks, with the track registry consumed by stop-review and governance checklists.
guarantees.automation: redcap-review-tracks-check.sh validates the three-track registry and confirms stop-review consumes it.

guarantees.rule: R0-R22 parent-task numbering must be machine-readable and must distinguish recovered evidence from reconstructed continuation items.
guarantees.automation: redcap-r0-r22-registry-check.sh validates contiguous R0-R22 coverage, required evidence paths, source type, confidence, status, and explicit boundaries; spec-check and diagnose consume it.

guarantees.rule: RedCap execution-layer physical migration must begin with a dry-run manifest that blocks direct apply, exposes path/hook/catalog impact, and requires rollback plans before any real move.
guarantees.automation: redcap-execution-layer-split-check.sh validates the dry-run manifest, rejects apply_allowed=true, requires safe targets, existing sources, non-empty rollback plans, high-risk blockers, and explicit P1-2 deferral; spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance consume it.

guarantees.rule: Historical docs, reports, knowledge, and runtime evidence migration must begin with a dry-run manifest that preserves archaeology, catalog links, receipt anchors, and rollback before any real move or delete.
guarantees.automation: redcap-legacy-asset-migration-check.sh validates asset collections, counts, actions, risks, apply status, catalog/link/rollback plans, and prism/runs retention summary; spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance consume it.

guarantees.rule: Historical asset migration real apply must not begin until a file-level preflight manifest proves no delete/move/public-export, preserves old anchors, and names catalog/link/receipt/rollback gates.
guarantees.automation: redcap-legacy-asset-migration-apply-plan.sh validates the file-level preflight manifest, blocks delete/move/public targets, rejects path traversal and duplicate targets, requires receipt-anchor guards, and is consumed by spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance.

guarantees.rule: Historical asset migration real apply must first pass a temp-copy or throwaway-worktree rehearsal proving copy-first hash equality, old-path retention, alias-map coverage, rollback-only cleanup, and no main-tree mutation.
guarantees.automation: redcap-legacy-asset-migration-rehearsal.sh runs the copy-first rehearsal in a temporary sandbox, rejects forbidden operations, traversal, public targets, duplicate targets and existing main-tree targets, validates alias-map and rollback counts, and is consumed by spec-check, diagnose, and acceptance.

guarantees.rule: Historical asset migration real apply must pass a true git-worktree rehearsal before any main-tree apply, proving copy-first can run in isolation while old docs catalog anchors, alias overlay, rollback and main-tree status remain safe.
guarantees.automation: redcap-legacy-asset-migration-worktree-rehearsal.sh creates a detached temporary git worktree, performs copy-first rehearsal there, validates old docs catalog anchors, alias overlay, rollback, stale-result detection and main-tree no-mutation, and is consumed by spec-check, diagnose and acceptance.

guarantees.rule: Historical asset migration must expose a durable old-path-authoritative alias resolver before any main-tree apply, so receipt anchors and docs catalog old paths remain resolvable while candidate redcap-knowledge targets are still planned.
guarantees.automation: redcap-legacy-asset-alias-resolver.sh validates the resolver against worktree rehearsal output and docs catalog, rejects stale results, duplicate paths, missing old anchors, path traversal, public targets and target hash mismatch, and is consumed by spec-check, diagnose and acceptance.

guarantees.rule: Parent task completion must be derived from an aggregation policy over completed child receipts and explicit not-complete boundaries, never from a single child receipt.
guarantees.automation: redcap-parent-receipt-aggregation-check.sh validates completed child evidence entries, locates matching runtime receipts, checks task_id/confirmed_hash/repo_path/report_path/status/promise_pending/acceptance_status/git head correspondence, validates not-complete reasons and next steps, and keeps parent_completion_allowed=false while open/blocked/resource-limited/deferred child items remain.

guarantees.rule: Hook, validator, and runtime contract hardening must be checked as executable contracts, not only as natural-language hook standards.
guarantees.automation: redcap-hook-contract-check.sh verifies hook standards, validator modes, stop-review, session-end, task-complete, and runtime helper linkage.

guarantees.rule: Common runtime attach/load patterns must converge on shared helpers in redcap-runtime-state.sh instead of being reimplemented across hook and validator scripts.
guarantees.automation: redcap-runtime-helper-check.sh ensures managed scripts use redcap_runtime_attach_current_or_claim and no longer define local attach helpers.

guarantees.rule: cli_console.md must remain a local-only overwrite display mirror and must not become a second answer log or repo-tracked truth surface.
guarantees.automation: redcap-cli-console-mirror-check.sh validates ignore status, artifact classification, and overwrite-only helper behavior.

guarantees.rule: Human-facing checkpoints and Feishu notifications must expose whether Norven needs to act, whether the task is blocked, whether the next step can start, the task panorama, and the current node. Reports must be conclusion-first and paragraph-readable, not a changelog of files/scripts. Internal audit gaps must be ledger-only by default, not Feishu noise.
guarantees.automation: redcap-human-communication-check.sh validates the shared status surface, Feishu formatter fields, SessionEnd audit-gap notification mute, and legacy hook notification mute.

manual_review_boundaries.reason: A hook can require a lesson check section, but it cannot safely decide whether a nuanced event deserves a permanent lesson without creating noisy memory.
Identity is a personal continuity asset; scripts may protect the workflow but must not auto-write personality conclusions.
Login state, rate limits, and API keys are local credentials; RedCap can sniff and report but should not silently repair or spend them.
Four-line status and terminology rules can be scaffolded and reviewed, but strict regex gates would misfire on commands, paths, field names, and quoted user text.

Whether the active host agent pauses, asks the user, or stops before commit is decided inside the host reply path. RedCap can constrain and audit this behavior, but without host-level reply veto or pre-send hooks it cannot honestly promise 100% physical enforcement.
